issues.should_be: The email states: 'Coming back from a friend's birthday party, where I had a few drinks, I lost control and hit a fence.' This is a sign of a possible exclusion under Article 3.1 ('the driver had alcohol above the legal limit, or was under the influence of drugs'), which must be flagged and referred to a claims handler under Article 7.2 — never applied or paid automatically. <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2-3" name="contract.pdf"/>
issues.evidence: Customer email: 'where I had a few drinks, I lost control and hit a fence' — a possible alcohol-related exclusion signal under contract Article 3.1 <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>, which Article 3/7.2 say must be referred to a handler <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2-3" name="contract.pdf"/>; recording it as null contradicts the email.

Deadline OK (incident 2026-10-21, reported 2026-10-22, within the 5 days of Article 4.1 <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>); coverage C2 is in the Policy Schedule <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>; required C2 documents (photos, repair quote) provided and received; the playbook commercial-vehicle referral rule is not triggered (email: no one else involved). However, the email states the driver 'had a few drinks' before losing control, a possible exclusion under Article 3.1; per Article 3 and Article 7.2 such a claim must be referred to a Veridia claims handler who decides — it must not be paid automatically, and the staged automatic payout (with exclusion_signal recorded as null) is therefore a concern. <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2-3" name="contract.pdf"/> (The assessor booking for 2026-10-25 is consistent with Article 6.1 since €1,800 > €1,500, and the €300 C2 deductible is correct as the driver is at fault and licence date 2008-11-01 means no young-driver surcharge under Article 5.3 <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>, but payment must wait for the handler's exclusion decision.)

checks.evidence: Customer email: 'I lost control and hit a fence'; contract Article 2 table C2 = 'Damage to the insured vehicle after a collision' <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>; Policy Schedule coverages include {"code": "C2", "name": "Collision damage"}.

checks.sources_say: Email: 'I lost control and hit a fence' — the policyholder caused the damage himself; no other driver involved, so the not-at-fault waiver of Article 5.2 does not apply and the standard C2 deductible stands. <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>
checks.evidence: Customer email: 'I lost control and hit a fence. No one else was involved.'; contract Article 5.2 not-at-fault waiver requires not at fault AND third party identified <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2" name="contract.pdf"/>.

checks.sources_say: Email: 'No one else was involved.' The playbook rule on commercial vehicles (van, truck, lorry, delivery vehicle) is not triggered because no other vehicle of any kind is involved.
checks.evidence: Customer email: 'No one else was involved.'; handler playbook commercial-vehicle referral rule therefore does not apply.

verdict.summary: Facts match the email and Policy Schedule, but the email's admission of 'a few drinks' before losing control is a possible alcohol exclusion (contract Article 3.1) that must be referred to a claims handler under Article 7.2, so the claim must not be paid automatically despite being reported on time, covered under C2, and fully documented.
